translations.literal: Day bingwu: at the hour of sunset the outer city fell.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, at sunset, the outer city fell.

sentences.zh: 是夕，皇后周氏崩。

translations.literal: That evening, Empress Zhou died.
translations.idiomatic: That evening Empress Zhou died.

sentences.zh: 丁未，昧爽，內城陷。

translations.literal: Day dingwei: at dawn the inner city fell.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, at dawn, the inner city fell.

sentences.zh: 帝崩于萬歲山，王承恩從死。

translations.literal: The emperor died on Wansui Hill; Wang Chen'en followed him in death.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor died on Wansui Hill; Wang Chen'en followed him in death.

sentences.zh: 御書衣襟曰：「朕涼德藐躬，上干天咎，然皆諸臣誤朕。

translations.literal: He wrote on his collar: "My meager virtue and slight person have offended Heaven, yet it is all my ministers who have misled me.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote on his collar: "My meager virtue and slight person have offended Heaven, yet it is all my ministers who have misled me.

sentences.zh: 朕死無面目見祖宗，自去冠冕，以發覆面。

translations.literal: At death I have no face to meet my ancestors; I therefore remove my crown and cover my face with my hair.
translations.idiomatic: At death I have no face to meet my ancestors; I therefore remove my crown and cover my face with my hair.

sentences.zh: 任賊分裂，無傷百姓一人。

translations.literal: Let the rebels dismember me as they will — do not harm a single one of my people."
translations.idiomatic: Let the rebels dismember me as they will — do not harm a single one of my people."

sentences.zh: 」自大學士范景文而下死者數十人。

translations.literal: From Grand Secretary Fan Jingwen downward, several tens died.
translations.idiomatic: From Grand Secretary Fan Jingwen downward, several tens were killed.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，賊遷帝、後梓宮於昌平。

translations.literal: Day bingchen: the rebels moved the imperial coffins of the Emperor and Empress to Changping.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen the rebels moved the imperial coffins of the Emperor and Empress to Changping.

sentences.zh: 昌平人啟田貴妃墓以葬。

translations.literal: The people of Changping opened Consort Tian's tomb for the burial.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Changping opened Consort Tian's tomb to receive them.

sentences.zh: 明亡。

translations.literal: The Ming perished.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming dynasty fell.

sentences.zh: 是年夏四月，我大清兵破賊於山海關，五月，入京師，以帝體改葬，令臣民為服喪三日，諡曰莊烈湣皇帝，陵曰思陵。

translations.literal: That year, in the fourth month of summer, our Great Qing troops defeated the rebels at Shanhai Pass; in the fifth month they entered the capital, reburied the Emperor's remains, ordered officials and commoners to observe mourning for three days, bestowed the posthumous title Emperor Zhuanglie Min, and named the mausoleum Siling.
translations.idiomatic: That summer, in the fourth month, our Great Qing armies broke the rebels at Shanhai Pass; in the fifth month they entered the capital, gave the Emperor a proper reburial, ordered officials and commoners to mourn for three days, posthumously titled him Emperor Zhuanglie Min, and named his tomb Siling.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：帝承神、熹之後，慨然有為。

translations.literal: Appraisal: The Emperor succeeded Shenzong and Xizong, and resolved to act boldly.
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal: The Emperor came to the throne after Shenzong and Xizong, and was stirred to bold action.

sentences.zh: 即位之初，沈機獨斷，刈除奸逆，天下想望治平。

translations.literal: At the beginning of his reign he pondered in secret and decided alone, cut down traitors and the wicked, and the realm looked to him for good order.
translations.idiomatic: Early in his reign he thought deeply and ruled on his own, swept away traitors and the wicked, and the realm looked to him for peace.

sentences.zh: 惜乎大勢已傾，積習難挽。

translations.literal: Alas, the great tide had already turned and entrenched habits were hard to reverse.
translations.idiomatic: Alas, the great tide had already turned, and long-standing abuses could not be undone.

sentences.zh: 在廷則門戶糾紛。

translations.literal: At court, factional cliques wrangled.
translations.idiomatic: At court, partisan factions wrangled without end.

sentences.zh: 疆埸則將驕卒惰。

translations.literal: On the frontiers, generals were arrogant and soldiers slack.
translations.idiomatic: On the frontiers, generals grew arrogant and soldiers grew slack.

sentences.zh: 兵荒四告，流寇蔓延。

translations.literal: War and famine were reported from all four quarters, and roving bandits spread everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: War and famine were reported from every quarter, and roving rebels spread everywhere.

sentences.zh: 遂至潰爛而莫可救，可謂不幸也已。

translations.literal: Thus affairs rotted to collapse beyond recovery—one may call it misfortune indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the state rotted to collapse beyond saving—a misfortune, indeed.

sentences.zh: 然在位十有七年，不邇聲色，憂勸惕勵，殫心治理。

translations.literal: Yet in seventeen years on the throne he did not draw near to music and beauty; he urged himself with anxious vigilance and devoted his heart to governance.
translations.idiomatic: Yet through seventeen years on the throne he kept clear of pleasure, drove himself with anxious vigilance, and gave his whole heart to rule.

sentences.zh: 臨朝浩歎，慨然思得非常之材，而用匪其人，益以僨事。

translations.literal: At court he sighed deeply, longing ardently for extraordinary talent, yet employed men who were not fit—and so only added to failed undertakings.
translations.idiomatic: At court he sighed aloud, yearning for extraordinary men, yet raised the unworthy to office—and so only piled failure upon failure.

sentences.zh: 乃復信任宦官，布列要地，舉措失當，制置乖方。

translations.literal: Then he again placed trust in eunuchs, stationed them at key posts, his measures went awry, and his arrangements were ill-suited.
translations.idiomatic: Then he trusted eunuchs again, posted them to vital posts, and with every move misjudged and every plan awry.

sentences.zh: 祚訖運移，身罹禍變，豈非氣數使然哉。

translations.literal: When his mandate ended and fortune shifted, he himself met calamity—was this not the decree of cosmic fate?
translations.idiomatic: When his mandate ran out and fortune turned, he himself met disaster—was this not Heaven's decree?

sentences.zh: 迨至大命有歸，妖氛盡掃，而帝得加諡建陵，典禮優厚。

translations.literal: When at last the Mandate found its home and demonic miasma was swept clean, the Emperor received a posthumous title and a mausoleum built for him, with ceremonies generously observed.
translations.idiomatic: When at last the Mandate had found its lord and the evil air was swept away, the Emperor was given a posthumous title and a tomb, with rites accorded in full generosity.

sentences.zh: 是則聖朝盛德，度越千古，亦可以知帝之蒙難而不辱其身，為亡國之義烈矣。

translations.literal: This shows the sage dynasty's abundant virtue, surpassing a thousand ages; from it one may know that though the Emperor suffered hardship he did not dishonor his person, and stands as a righteous martyr among fallen dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: In this the sage dynasty's virtue shines beyond all ages; and one may see that though the Emperor suffered calamity, he did not dishonor himself—he stands as the righteous martyr of a fallen realm.
